Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

Title: Diagnosis

Details: The failing test `testUnion` verifies that the union of two XPath expressions returns nodes in document order, regardless of the order of the unioned paths. Specifically, it checks that "/vendor[1]/contact[1] | /vendor[1]/contact[4]" and "/vendor[1]/contact[4] | /vendor[1]/contact[1]" both yield the string value "John" from the correct document-ordered node.

The related bug report describes that the core union operation does not correctly sort result nodes in document order, leading to incorrect string-value extraction when the union's resulting node set is not sorted. This violates the XPath specification that the string-value of a node set is the value of the first node in document order.

Investigation of method names related to union operation (e.g., "union") in the JXPath codebase did not yield a direct implementation in the searched classes. However, the evidence suggests that the union operation returns a node set that is not sorted properly before being returned or used.

Therefore, the root cause is that the union operation in the XPath implementation fails to ensure the result nodes are sorted by document order, a requirement for correct XPath evaluation semantics. This leads to inconsistencies such as picking the wrong node's string value, as in the example: "string(/MAIN/B | /MAIN/A)" returns "bvalue" instead of "avalue".

This bug manifests when the union operation returns nodes in the order they are found or unioned rather than their document order.

The fix should ensure node sets resulting from union operations are sorted by document order before they are returned or further processed.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
